calls.head: Utah’s shot volume meets a soft spot
calls.body: Utah ranks 5th of 32 for shot volume (60.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5); Chicago ranks 29th for shot suppression.
calls.call: Utah takes at least its usual 60.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Utah took 73.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against its usual 60.3.

calls.head: Different shooting spots
calls.body: On point-shot reliance, Chicago sits 12th of 32, at the point-heavy end of the scale. Utah is 32nd, at the down low end.
calls.call: Chicago takes a bigger share of its shots from the point than Utah.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shot attempts from the point, Chicago had 53% and Utah 31%. Coming in, Chicago was at 42% and Utah at 38%.

UTA.head: We gave Utah a 66% chance, and Utah delivered.

CHI.head: We gave Chicago only a 34% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Utah brought the hits
surprises.body: Utah’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 204, against its usual 93 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 200 games.
